name: Convert a coal-fired boiler unit to natural gas
summary: This process converts one coal-fired steam unit of about 400 MW to burn natural gas so it can keep running past the coal phase-out with roughly half the carbon intensity. A conversion project manager frames the scope, engineers fix a design basis, the regulatory group obtains amended AUC and environmental approvals, supply chain buys burners and controls, and the unit is converted during a planned outage that is combined with its major maintenance, then commissioned and tested. Most of the elapsed time is waiting: about a year for approvals, months of equipment lead time, and the wait for the unit's turn in the spring or fall outage calendar because units are converted one at a time.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator converting three wholly owned coal units at two Wabamun-area plants to gas in 2020-2021, with a small energy transition project team, plant engineers and contracted boiler and controls vendors.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the Sundance 6, Keephills 2 and Keephills 3 conversions (completed February, July and December 2021) and a peer's Genesee dual-fuel work. Partner-operated units are out of scope.

trigger: The strategic plan names a coal unit for conversion to gas.
end_state: The unit runs commercially on gas, its capability and emissions are tested, it is handed to operations and the project is closed; or the conversion is deferred at the investment decision.

volume.seasonality: Conversion outages fall in the spring and fall low-price outage seasons; the three wholly owned conversions ran in overlapping phases from mid-2018 to December 2021 and none started after.

evidence.note: Three wholly owned units converted in 2021 (src1, src2) over a 2019-2022 window of 48 months is about 0.06 projects a month; the high end allows for units evaluated but not converted (Keephills 1, Sundance 3-5).

Two to three conversion project managers ran the three conversions in parallel phases in 2019-2021; share estimated. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40: benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent).

systems.name: Document management and engineering drawings repository
Outage and project scheduling software (critical path)
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
AER and Alberta Environment submission portals

resources.name: Gas-fired steam unit converted from coal (about 400 to 460 MW)

steps.name: Frame conversion scope and business case
steps.description: The conversion project manager takes the unit named in the strategic plan, gathers its boiler data, fan curves and remaining-life studies from the document store, and builds a spreadsheet case comparing gas cost, carbon cost and added unit life against the conversion capital. The output is a scope note and a request for a feasibility study.

error.defect_description: Scope misses an upgrade the unit needs on gas (fan capacity, controls).

evidence.note: Conversion rationale (life extension of 8 to 10 years, halved intensity) in src1; boiler-conversion scope in src5. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Wait for the feasibility study
steps.description: An engineering consultant or the boiler manufacturer models gas firing in the existing furnace: burner count and size, heat absorption, steam temperatures, fan duty and flue gas temperature. The project waits for the study report.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Typical duration of a front-end boiler conversion study; author estimate.

steps.name: Review the study and fix the design basis
steps.description: The plant engineer checks the study against operating data from the historian, questions assumptions on steam temperatures and tube metal limits, and writes the design basis: number of burners, gas flow, minimum stable load and which coal equipment is left in place. If the study is unconvincing it goes back to the consultant.

error.defect_description: Design basis understates a gas-firing effect such as higher superheat temperatures.

evidence.note: src5 lists the modified and new equipment and notes no heat-rate improvement. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Prepare technical content for the regulatory amendments
steps.description: The project manager writes the technical sections for an amendment of the power plant approval at the Alberta Utilities Commission and of the environmental approval held under EPEA: fuel change, expected NOx and CO2 rates, noise and any new gas facilities. It is sent as a filing request to the regulatory group.

error.defect_description: Emission or equipment details incomplete, prompting information requests.

evidence.note: src4: amendment applications filed with the AUC and AEP in summer 2018. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: File the amendment applications
steps.description: The regulatory affairs advisor assembles the applications, checks them against the commission's power plant rules and the environmental approval conditions, files them through AUC eFiling and the Alberta Environment submission portal, and handles public notice.

error.defect_description: Filing deficiency returned by the regulator.

control.basis: AUC approval of power plant amendments (Hydro and Electric Energy Act) and EPEA approval amendment

evidence.note: Applications to both regulators in src4; AUC approvals in src5. Detailed filing work sits in hse-regulatory-filings.

steps.name: Regulators review the applications
steps.description: The AUC and Alberta Environment and Parks review the applications, post notice and decide whether to ask questions. The project waits; about six in ten conversions draw information requests.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Summer 2018 filing to December 2018 AUC approval (about 5 months, src5) and to July 2019 AEP final approval (about 12 months, src4). Share with questions is an estimate.

steps.name: Answer information requests
steps.description: The project manager drafts answers to the regulators' questions with input from the plant engineer, for example on NOx emission rates during start-up or on the gas lateral, and the regulatory advisor files them.

error.defect_description: An answer raises a further question.

control.basis: AUC and AEP information request process

evidence.note: Common practice in AUC and EPEA proceedings; author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for final approvals
steps.description: The project waits for the AUC approval and the amended EPEA approval to be issued, with conditions on emission limits and monitoring that the design must meet.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: AEP final approvals came about 7 months after the AUC approval (src4, src5).

steps.name: Approve the investment and issue notice to proceed
steps.description: The director of energy transition presents the cost estimate, schedule and regulatory conditions to the executive team and, above the delegated limit, to the board, then issues the notice to proceed. Some units are deferred or dropped at this point.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: capital above the executive limit needs board approval

evidence.note: Final Notice to Proceed for Sundance 6 in July 2019 (src5), the month AEP approvals were final; Keephills 1 and Sundance 3-4 were still under evaluation (src5). Deferral share estimated.

steps.name: Tender and award burner, controls and construction contracts
steps.description: The supply contract specialist issues requests for proposals for gas burners and igniters, burner management and DCS changes, and construction labour, runs the bid evaluation with the project team and awards the contracts in the ERP.

error.defect_description: Scope gap between burner supplier and installer.

control.basis: Competitive bidding and award approval under the procurement policy

evidence.note: Emerson held controls contracts for four units (src5). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Wait for burner and controls supply
steps.description: The burner maker designs, builds and ships the burners, igniters, flame scanners, valve trains and piping, and the controls supplier configures the new burner management logic. The project waits for delivery while engineering work proceeds.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: vendor drawings issued; manufacturing under way

evidence.note: Manufacturing lead time for custom burner sets and valve trains; author estimate. Wait reduced to allow for engineering touch time that runs during it.

steps.name: Arrange firm gas service and the lateral tie-in
steps.description: The project manager agrees gas delivery capacity, pressure and the plant tie-in point with the pipeline operator, signs the service order and coordinates the meter station design with the gas buyer in marketing.

error.defect_description: Delivery pressure or capacity mismatched with burner needs.

evidence.note: Pioneer Pipeline supplied gas to Keephills and Sundance (src4) from May 2019 (src5). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Wait for the pipeline lateral and meter station
steps.description: The pipeline operator builds or extends the lateral and meter station to the plant fence. Most of this runs during the burner lead time; the wait here is only the part that runs past it.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Pipeline built ahead of the conversions (src5); residual wait estimated.

steps.name: Review vendor design and run the hazard review
steps.description: The plant engineer reviews vendor drawings, logic diagrams and the gas piping design, leads a hazard and operability review with operations and the vendors, and raises the engineering change that updates drawings, procedures and alarm settings.

error.defect_description: A HAZOP action is closed on paper but not built.

control.basis: Company management-of-change and process hazard analysis standard for new fuel systems

evidence.note: Standard practice for introducing a new fuel to a boiler; author estimate. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Register the fuel gas piping design with ABSA
steps.description: The plant engineer's package for the new gas piping and pressure parts is submitted to ABSA, the provincial pressure equipment authority, for design registration. The project waits for the registration number before fabrication of affected parts.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Alberta Pressure Equipment Safety Regulation: design registration before construction

evidence.note: ABSA design registration practice from general knowledge; source not opened.

steps.name: Fit the conversion into the outage plan
steps.description: The outage manager adds the conversion work packages to the unit's planned outage in the scheduling software, aligns them with the major maintenance scope and the crane plan, and confirms the outage window with the market and AESO outage reporting groups.

error.defect_description: Work fronts clash in the boiler during the outage.

evidence.note: Conversions combined with scheduled major maintenance (src2) and done in scheduled outages (src6). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Supervise pre-outage construction
steps.description: While the unit still runs on coal, the capital project manager supervises contractors installing gas piping from the meter station to the boiler house, cable trays and new control cabinets, checking progress, safety and quality daily.

error.defect_description: Pre-outage work incomplete when the outage starts.

control.basis: Prime contractor and permit-to-work requirements under the Alberta OHS Act and Code

evidence.note: Wait is contractor mobilisation. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Shut the unit down and isolate the coal systems
steps.description: At the start of the planned outage window the shift supervisor brings the unit off line, isolates and locks out the coal mills, feeders and conveyors (left in place), and issues the permits that let contractors enter the boiler.

error.defect_description: Isolation point missed on a coal system.

control.basis: Permit-to-work and lockout (Alberta OHS Code Part 15)

evidence.note: Units were taken one outage at a time: Sundance 6 done Feb 2021, Keephills 2 mid-2021, Keephills 3 Dec 2021 (src2), and coal equipment left in place (src5). The long calendar wait is the sequencing of units into spring and fall outage windows.

steps.name: Install gas burners, igniters, scanners and fuel trains
steps.description: The project manager directs the boiler contractor removing coal burners and fitting gas burners, igniters, flame scanners, valve trains and windbox changes, tracks the critical path daily and resolves interferences found when the boiler is opened. The unit stays off line throughout.

error.defect_description: Installation defect in a burner or valve train.

control.basis: Confined space entry and hot work permits (Alberta OHS Code)

evidence.note: Scope in src5; outage of 'just a couple of months' (src5); up to 700-800 extra workers at peak (src2, src3). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Carry out the scheduled major maintenance in the same outage
steps.description: The specialist crew lead runs the turbine, valve and generator inspections booked for the same outage, using the turbine hall crane, so that the unit returns with both the new fuel system and its overhaul done.

error.defect_description: Reassembly finding delays start-up.

control.basis: Permit-to-work and lockout (Alberta OHS Code Part 15)

evidence.note: Sundance 6 and Keephills 2 budgets included scheduled major maintenance (src2, src3). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Install and loop-check the burner management and DCS changes
steps.description: Instrument and electrical technicians wire the new flame scanners, valves and transmitters, load the new burner management logic with the controls vendor, and check every loop from field device to control room screen.

error.defect_description: Wrong scanner or trip setting.

control.basis: Burner management practice under NFPA 85 as adopted in company standards

evidence.note: Burner management system reconfiguration and control upgrades in src5; NFPA 85 basis is the author's general knowledge. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: ABSA inspection and pressure test sign-off
steps.description: An ABSA-authorised inspector witnesses the pressure test of the new gas piping and reviews the inspection records before the system may be put into service. The project waits for the inspector's visit and sign-off.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Alberta Safety Codes Act and Pressure Equipment Safety Regulation inspection before operation

evidence.note: ABSA inspection practice from general knowledge; source not opened.

steps.name: Pre-start safety review and operator training
steps.description: The shift supervisor walks down the new system against the HAZOP actions and checklists, confirms isolations are removed, and trains each operating crew on the new start-up sequence and trips before first fire.

error.defect_description: Crew on a later rotation not trained before start-up.

control.basis: Pre-startup safety review in the company process safety standard

evidence.note: Common practice for a fuel change; crews work rotating shifts, so training spans several days.

steps.name: First fire on gas and tune the burners
steps.description: The plant engineer leads first fire with the burner vendor, raises load in steps, and tunes air and fuel ratios against flame scanner signals, steam temperatures and CEMS NOx readings. About three in ten units hit a problem that needs fixing before tuning can finish.

error.defect_description: Tuning leaves NOx near the approval limit.

next.condition: trips, flame instability or temperature limits

evidence.note: Commissioning practice for boiler conversions; share needing fixes estimated.

steps.name: Fix commissioning defects
steps.description: The project manager gets the vendor or contractor to correct the defect found at first fire, such as a scanner position, a valve trip setting or a leaking flange, and arranges the re-test.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Wait is for a vendor technician or parts; author estimate.

steps.name: Run capability, emissions and federal performance tests
steps.description: The plant engineer runs the capacity test needed to declare the unit's gas capability to the market operator, checks the CEMS against reference tests, and plans the federal initial performance test that an independent verifier must witness within twelve months.

error.defect_description: Test result recorded at the wrong conditions.

control.basis: SOR/2018-261 ss. 5 and 22: initial performance test within 12 months with independent verifier

evidence.note: Test timing and verifier requirement in src7 ss. 5 and 22; the market capability test is handed to eng-performance-testing.

steps.name: Declare the unit available on gas and hand over
steps.description: The project manager hands the unit to plant operations with the updated drawings, procedures and engineering change closed, and confirms the new capability and emission rates for the market and emissions teams.

error.defect_description: Drawings not updated for a field change.

evidence.note: Units declared converted with unchanged nameplate (src1). Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

steps.name: Close out the project
steps.description: The project manager reconciles final costs against budget in the ERP, settles contractor claims, archives as-built drawings and records lessons for the next unit's conversion, then closes the project.

error.defect_description: Late contractor claim after close.

evidence.note: Close-out typically waits for final contractor invoices; author estimate. Touch is the role's total hands-on hours over the phase, estimated from project size (35 to 96 million CAD per unit in src2/src3).

exceptions.name: Information requests from regulators
exceptions.description: The AUC or AEP asks questions on emissions, noise or gas facilities, adding a response round before approval.

exceptions.name: Commissioning defect
exceptions.description: First fire reveals a scanner, trip-setting or valve problem that the vendor must fix before tuning can finish, holding the unit off line longer.

exceptions.name: Study revision
exceptions.description: The plant engineer rejects the feasibility study's assumptions and it goes back to the consultant.

exceptions.name: Deferred at investment decision
exceptions.description: The executive team or board defers the unit, as happened with units that stayed under evaluation.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the strategic decision to handover on gas
benchmarks.population: Three Alberta 395-463 MW coal-to-gas boiler conversions, 2018-2021

evidence.note: Applications filed summer 2018 (src4); Sundance 6 complete Feb 2021 (about 31 months) and Keephills 2 July 2021 (about 36 months) (src2, src1); about 6 months of pre-application work added as a tier C estimate. Three cases only.

benchmarks.population: Simple boiler conversions to gas firing

evidence.note: src5 describes the turnaround as 'just a couple of months'; range estimated.

pain_points.description: Approvals from two regulators take about a year and set the earliest date for the investment decision.

evidence.note: Summer 2018 filings, December 2018 AUC and July 2019 AEP approvals.

pain_points.description: Units must wait for a planned outage window and are converted one at a time to keep capacity in the market and spread crews, so later units wait more than a year after their equipment arrives.

evidence.note: Sundance 6, Keephills 2 and Keephills 3 completed six months apart (src2).

pain_points.description: Seven to eight hundred extra workers on site at peak make the outage a contractor safety and coordination load for a small project team.

evidence.note: Nearly 700 (Sundance 6) and 800 (Keephills 2) extra jobs at peak.

pain_points.description: COVID-19 restrictions in 2020-2021 put outage staffing and schedules at risk.

evidence.note: COVID-19 named as a conversion schedule assumption and risk in src2.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Sundance 6 conversion announced complete 1 Feb 2021, Keephills 2 on 19 Jul 2021, all three (KH2 395 MW, KH3 463 MW, Sun6 401 MW) by 29 Dec 2021; intensity falls from about 1.04-1.05 to 0.51-0.52 t CO2e/MWh (KH3 0.86 to 0.43); 8 to 10 years of added life; Sheerness 2 converted 4 Apr 2020 and Sheerness 1 on 31 Mar 2021 (partner-operated); federal standard of 0.420 t CO2e/MWh for gas units above 150 MW.

sources.title: TransAlta Completes First Off-Coal Conversion and Achieves Major Milestone in Phase Out of Coal
sources.supports: Sundance 6: 35 million CAD boiler conversion plus 50 million CAD DCS upgrade and scheduled major maintenance (85 million total); nearly 700 extra jobs at peak; Keephills 2 expected mid-June 2021 and Keephills 3 mid-December 2021; COVID-19 named as a schedule risk.

sources.title: TransAlta Completes Second Off-Coal Conversion - Another Major Milestone in its Phase Out of Coal
sources.supports: Keephills 2: 31.5 million CAD conversion plus 64.7 million CAD system upgrades, gas infrastructure and maintenance (over 96 million total); nearly 800 extra jobs at peak; nameplate unchanged at 395 MW.

sources.title: TransAlta Completes Second Coal-to-Gas Conversion
sources.supports: Amendment applications filed with the AUC and Alberta Environment and Parks in summer 2018; AEP final approvals July 2019; Pioneer Pipeline built with Tidewater supplies gas to both plants and was later sold to ATCO for 255 million CAD.

sources.title: Gas breathes new life into aging coal plants
sources.supports: AUC approved basic conversions of Sundance 3-6 and Keephills 1-2 in December 2018 and Keephills 3 in February 2019; Final Notice to Proceed for Sundance 6 in July 2019 with the outage in the second half of 2020; a simple boiler conversion is a turnaround of 'just a couple of months'; scope is new gas burners, igniters, scanners, piping and valves with modified fans, boiler and controls; coal handling decommissioned in place; Emerson reconfiguring the burner management system; no heat-rate improvement; Pioneer pipeline delivering gas from May 2019.

sources.title: Capital Power accelerates plans for natural gas capability at the Genesee facility
sources.supports: A peer Alberta generator converts Genesee 1 and 2 to dual fuel during regularly scheduled maintenance outages for about 50 million CAD over 2019-2021, subject to regulatory approvals, with on-site gas pipeline infrastructure and boiler modifications.

sources.title: Regulations Limiting Carbon Dioxide Emissions from Natural Gas-fired Generation of Electricity (SOR/2018-261)
sources.publisher: Government of Canada, Justice Laws Website
sources.supports: Applies to boiler units converted from coal from 1 January of the year after coal firing stops (s. 3(4)); initial performance test within 12 months (s. 5) of at least two hours; performance test report within 60 days with an independent verifier's report for the initial test (s. 22); limit of 420 t CO2/GWh deferred according to the initial test result (s. 4(2)).

assumptions: One case is one unit conversion project from the strategic decision to close-out. The organisation file counts 'project-months' (1 to 5 a month); this file counts projects (three in 2019-2022), so its volume is about 0.07 a month.

Touch time on long project steps is the role's total hands-on hours over that phase. Because the simulator adds touch time to elapsed time as round-the-clock minutes, wait times on long phases (vendor lead time, outage calendar) were reduced so that wait plus touch roughly matches the dates in the sources. Concurrent outage steps (s19 to s21) are summed by the simulator, which approximates a 60 to 90 day outage.

The converted_gas_unit resource is listed without a running cost because the unit burns no fuel while it is off line for conversion; the economic cost of the outage is lost market margin, which is not modelled here.
Contractor craft labour (700 to 800 workers at peak) and vendor engineers are outside parties and appear only as waits or as the work the project manager and crew lead supervise.

The regulatory filing itself is documented in hse-regulatory-filings; this file includes only the project's share (technical content, filing and answers) and the waits on the regulators. The regulatory approval is listed as an input, not a trigger, because it arrives in the middle of a case.

ABSA design registration and inspection, NFPA 85 burner management practice and the OHS Code permit rules are named from general knowledge; those sources were not opened, so those steps are tier C or B on other grounds.

The simulated median (about 1,230 days) is about 7 percent above the 1,150-day benchmark built from three conversions, inside the spread between Sundance 6 and Keephills 2; the dates of Keephills 3's applications were not found. Staffing stated (3.0 FTE across roles) is above the 2.2 FTE implied by touch time because project staff also carry coordination time not written as steps.
